title: Chicken drumstick, rotisserie, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken drumsticks cooked on a rotisserie are the thigh meat of the bird, usually served without skin. Rotisserie cooking provides even heat and a characteristic smoky flavor. The meat is tender, juicy, high in protein and relatively low in fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks are a staple in fast‑food and street‑food dishes.
Rotisserie cooking requires little added oil, making the product leaner.
Chicken was domesticated over 8,000 years ago and is one of the most widely kept livestock species.
Removing the skin cuts saturated fat content, creating a more diet‑friendly option.
Dark meat contains more iron than white breast meat.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Drumsticks provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The product contains virtually no carbs, suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken supplies vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: It provides zinc, phosphorus and iron, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Reduced fat when skin is removed
items.content: Skipping the skin dramatically lowers saturated fat and calorie content.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken meat.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter.

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: Pre‑seasoned drumsticks often contain added salt, increasing sodium intake.

items.title: Cholesterol if skin is eaten
items.content: Consuming the skin raises saturated fat and cholesterol levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Skin‑less drumsticks can be eaten hot, added to salads, soups, stews, or used in sandwiches. They are easy to slice for quick‑prep meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C up to 3 months. Ensure the meat is thoroughly reheated before consumption.
